correctness.rationale: For compact scaled ranks, exact binomial and two-coordinate multinomial formulas imply the random class intensities converge in L1 at rate \(O(n^{-\gamma/2}+n^{\gamma-1})\); the diagonal variance is \(O(n^{-\gamma})\) and cross-label covariances are \(O(n^{-1})\). Explicit \(e^{-np_j/2}\) binomial bounds justify uniform rank-tail truncation. The probability of any relevant repeated future label is \(O(n^{-\gamma})\), enabling exact one-draw conditional Laplace factorization. Its Taylor and Riemann errors are \(O(n^{\gamma-1})\), yielding quenched marked Poisson convergence with the stated compact Lipschitz rate. The y=cx^{-a} Jacobian gives \(\mathrm{Gamma}(r-\gamma,1)\). The included standard-library checker passed 1710 exact/numerical assertions, which do not stand in for the asymptotic proof.

The new 2026 outer-measure Gaussian field concerns large time segments, not the marked microscopic record problem. value.rationale: Label-popularity composition of short-window rare species arrivals is mathematically and statistically natural: time-only occupancy record laws do not tell whether new or r-th seen species came from comparatively common versus exceptionally rare labels. The mark law changes systematically from Gamma(1-gamma,1) to Gamma(r-gamma,1), is independent of the uniform event-time mark, and comes with a concrete conditional finite-window Laplace accuracy estimate. This supplies information for ranked-vocabulary sampling and conditional rare-event inference, not merely a renamed count theorem.
